endpoint.name: people.email.verify — routed: best of 11 providers, own keys first
endpoint.summary: Verify an email address — treg picks the provider (own keys first, then cheapest) and names the one that served

cost.note: NOT free: misses are billed too. the children's range $0–$0.0138 per hit, 0% markup; you pay the child that served AND every child tried before it that bills a miss (4 of 11 do), up to X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost (default $1 a call). X-Treg-Route-Exclude them, or X-Treg-Route-Waterfall: 0, to pay for one provider only

input.note: Send everything you know about the subject — treg derives the rest (full_name ⇄ first+last), matches each provider on the variants it accepts ({email}) and sends each provider only the fields it wants. On a miss treg keeps trying providers, cheapest first, within X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost (default $1 per call; misses on per-success providers are free). Options ride as headers, never in the body: X-Treg-Route-Waterfall: 0 (stop at the first miss), X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost: <usd>, X-Treg-Route-Prefer / X-Treg-Route-Exclude: <provider>. The response is {output, raw, _treg: {served_by, tried}}; X-Treg-Served-By names the child.

endpoint.capability_description: Check an email address you ALREADY have is real and deliverable — not for finding one

valid.note: the provider says the mailbox accepts mail

status.note: the provider's own verdict word (valid | invalid | accept_all | unknown | …)

headers.X-Treg-Route-Waterfall: on by default: a miss tries the next provider; 0 = stop at the first miss
headers.X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost: USD ceiling for the whole call (default 1.00)
headers.X-Treg-Route-Strict-Filters: 1 = never call a provider that cannot apply a filter you sent (answers 422, nothing charged); off by default — the answer names what was ignored in X-Treg-Ignored-Filters
